'''Laura Monk''' is a French mathematician whose research in [[spectral geometry]], on the [[Expander graph|expansion]] and [[Spectral shape analysis|spectral]] properties of random [[hyperbolic surface]]s, continues the work of [[Maryam Mirzakhani]].{{r|q}} She works in England at the [[University of Bristol]] as a Royal Society Dorothy Hodgkin Research Fellow and proleptic (tenure-track) [[Academic ranks in the United Kingdom|lecturer]].{{r|profile|cv}}

==Education and career==
After preparatory studies at the [[Lycée privé Sainte-Geneviève]], Monk received bachelor's degrees in both mathematics and physics at [[Paris-Sud University]] in 2015, passed her [[agrégation]] in mathematics in 2017, and received a master's degree with honors in 2018, also including study at the [[École Normale Supérieure]].{{r|cv}} She completed her Ph.D. in 2021 at the [[University of Strasbourg]], with the dissertation ''Geometry and spectrum of typical hyperbolic surfaces'' supervised by [[Nalini Anantharaman]].{{r|cv|these}}

She was a postdoctoral fellow at the [[Max Planck Institute for Mathematics]], working there with [[Ursula Hamenstädt]], from 2021 to 2022. She joined the University of Bristol in 2022 as a research associate of [[Jens Marklof]]. She became a research fellow and proleptic lecturer in 2024.{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
As a doctoral student, Monk was named a French Young Talent in the 2021 [[L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science Awards]].{{r|cv|fyt}} She was a 2024 recipient of the [[Maryam Mirzakhani New Frontiers Prize]], given to her "for advancing our understanding of random hyperbolic surfaces of large genus".{{r|nfp}}

The [[Royal Society]] awarded Monk a Dorothy Hodgkin Fellowship in 2024.{{r|hodgkin}}
